title: Kestrel and the Bakery
premise: Paloma Ravensworth has kept her heart on a strict training regimen since her father's bakery was seized in a predatory foreclosure a decade ago — and since her best friend and secret love, Theo Kestrel, stood silently by while it happened. Now her own café is three missed payments from the same fate, and the festival weekend that could save it is buried under a snowstorm that strands her with Theo and his business rival, Marguerite Voss, the heiress whose family bought Ravensworth's bakery. As the storm forces the three of them into the shuttered old bakery itself, Paloma discovers Marguerite has spent years quietly funding legal aid for foreclosed businesses, carrying her own guilt, and Theo has been hiding evidence that could overturn her father's seizure. In the festival's final hour, Paloma must say the sentence she has rehearsed for ten years — 'I forgive you, and I choose you' — to Theo, and together the three turn the bakery into a co-op that keeps her café, her memory, and her found family alive.
about_author: Juniper Okafor is the pen name of a former line cook who traded twelve-hour kitchen shifts for twelve-hour writing shifts and never noticed the difference. She lives above a bakery she cannot walk past without buying something, and writes romances about people who mistake stubbornness for self-protection.

chapters.title: Three Payments from Gone
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Opening the café before dawn, Paloma counts the till against the bank's final notice while the winter festival — her last chance at solvency — sets up outside. Theo Kestrel arrives with a sponsorship offer she can't afford to refuse and can't afford to accept, given their decade of silence. The beat: brittle pride masking terror, and the first crack in her rehearsed composure.

chapters.title: The Storm Locks the Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, shifting to Theo's mid-chapter. The blizzard strands festival vendors, and Marguerite Voss — Theo's rival and the heiress to the firm that foreclosed on Paloma's father — takes shelter in the derelict Ravensworth bakery. Trapped among her childhood ovens, Paloma discovers Marguerite's hidden ledger of quiet legal-aid donations. The beat: enemies thawing into uneasy alliance as old grief meets unexpected contrition.

chapters.title: What Theo Buried
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered by the storm and Marguerite's growing closeness to Paloma, Theo confesses he has held for years the misfiled documents proving the foreclosure was fraudulent — evidence he suppressed to protect his own career and Marguerite's family. Paloma's fury nearly ends everything, but Marguerite offers to testify, risking her inheritance. The beat: the climax — betrayal detonating into the choice between justice and safety.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Finally Spoken
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the festival's final morning, the roads clear; the three present the evidence, and the co-op plan for the old bakery is born. Before the crowds return, Paloma says the rehearsed sentence — 'I forgive you, and I choose you' — and kisses Theo among the flour dust. The beat: release and warmth; the heart, finally, off its training regimen.
